lawRefs: Local Tax Enabling Act, 53 P.S. § 6924.101 et seq. (local earned income tax)
header.notes: sha256 is of the canonical JSON body (JSON.stringify of the file without `header`). Values hand-transcribed; sha256 is of the canonical body. Rate: Pennsylvania personal income tax is "levied at the rate of 3.07 percent" on eight separate classes of income (compensation; interest; dividends; net profits; net gains from dispositions of property; rents and royalties; estates and trusts; gambling and lottery winnings). There is no standard deduction and no personal exemption. Pennsylvania does NOT start from federal AGI; startingPoint is set to federalAGI as the closest approximation (notable differences: employee elective deferrals to 401(k)-type plans and traditional IRA contributions are not deductible; no itemized deductions; losses in one class cannot offset income in another). Social Security and railroad retirement benefits are not taxable (PA Personal Income Tax Guide, Gross Compensation: https://www.pa.gov/agencies/revenue/forms-and-publications/pa-personal-income-tax-guide/gross-compensation.html). Retirement income: distributions from eligible retirement plans after retirement age are not taxable; early distributions are taxable to the extent they exceed previously taxed contributions (minAge 59 approximates this; the actual test is the plan's retirement age or 59 1/2 for IRAs). Capital gains are fully taxable at 3.07% with no long-term preference. The tax forgiveness credit for low incomes is not modeled. NOT MODELED: local earned income taxes on wages and net profits (and the Philadelphia wage tax), which do not apply to investment or retirement income. Cross-checked against Tax Foundation, "State Individual Income Tax Rates and Brackets, 2026" (data as of Jan 1 2026, updated Feb 11 2026).

flags.retirementIncomeExclusion: simplified: all eligible retirement-plan income exempt after plan retirement age / 59 1/2; early distributions taxable above basis
flags.startingPoint: approximation: Pennsylvania uses its own eight-class gross income base, not federal AGI (401(k) deferrals and IRA contributions are taxed when contributed)
